Subject: POC Trial: workload intake & next steps

Hi Alice,

Great to meet you and the team earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we can get the POC scoped and scheduled: 

Recap / Success criteria (from conversation)
- Functionality: Redwood must handle AcmeHealth's summarization pipeline end-to-end with >= 95% availability during business hours.
- Latency: 95th percentile in-line with target of < 300ms per request for text-only requests.
- Cost/throughput: Demonstrate predictable per-token economics at target throughput.
- Quality: Summaries should match your rubric (recall/precision thresholds we discussed) across the provided eval set.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Intake: Receive workload profile (RPS, token lengths, concurrency, burst windows) - see attached intake spreadsheet.
- Test window: 2-week trial run with progressive load testing (week 1 baseline, week 2 ramp + bursts).
- Metrics: latency, error rate, token cost, and quality on eval prompts.
- Kickoff: propose initial kickoff/check-in week of 9/6; target POC start 9/13 if intake complete.

Ownership / next steps
- Action for AcmeHealth: fill the attached "acme-poc-workload-intake.xlsx" with the traffic numbers below and return by EOD 9/3. Include IT contact for network/settings.
- Action for Redwood: we'll provision a sandbox project, prepare a baseline model config, and draft the mutual action plan once we have the intake. Marissa will drive orchestration; Dylan will size the infra.

Workload fields we need (quick checklist)
- Expected steady-state RPS and expected peak RPS
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + expected completion) and distribution (percentiles or typical buckets)
- Concurrency targets (simultaneous requests you expect)
- Typical burst patterns (time-of-day, day-of-week, end-of-quarter spikes)
- Any JWT/SSO/network egress requirements; IP allowlist needed?
- Data sensitivity (PHI/PII) and whether sample data can be shared for evaluation

Attached: acme-poc-workload-intake.xlsx (spreadsheet) - please return with fields filled.

If that works, we can lock the kickoff slot and get Dylan to start the infra sizing. Thanks again - looking forward to getting this moving.

Ben Carter

Ben,

Thanks for the clear recap. Attached is a short PDF summary of our workload profile; below are the quick answers in-line as well. We've reviewed with our IT/infra folks and are comfortable with the proposed evaluation plan.

Workload summary (high level)
- Steady-state RPS: 20-30 requests/sec across peak hours.
- Peak RPS: up to ~75 RPS during scheduled batch runs and morning peak (8:00-10:30am PT).
- Avg tokens per request: ~350 tokens (prompt 120 tokens + completion ~230 tokens).
- Token length distribution: 50th=300, 75th=420, 95th=800 (we've included a small tail for long-form queries).
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 10-25, but bursts can push to 100 concurrent requests for 5-20 minute windows.
- Burst patterns: daily morning spike, weekly Monday ramp, and end-of-quarter reporting spikes (last 3 days of each quarter).
- Data sensitivity: data is de-identified patient summaries; still governed - we'll need SOC2 evidence and a DPIA confirmation.
- IT contact: it-support@acmehealth.com (they're cc'd).
- Timeline: we prefer POC start the week of 9/13 and a 2-week data-collection run.

Attachments: acme-workload-profile.pdf (includes a small sample load chart and token distribution CSV).

I'll fill the attached spreadsheet and return it by Friday 9/3. Please include Marissa on scheduling.

Best,
